column3: NASB supplies “he said” before Eliezer’s words.
“for Israel’s sake” renders “on account of Israel,” and “the Egyptians” renders “Egypt.”
NASB supplies “it was proven” and “the people” to complete a terse clause, “for in the matter in which they acted presumptuously against them”; the meaning is uncertain.
“When they have a dispute” renders “when there is a matter for them.”
“You will surely wear out” renders an emphatic doubled verb; “the task” renders “the thing.”
“You be the people’s representative before God” renders “be you for the people in front of God.”
“So it will be easier for you” renders “lighten from upon yourself,” and NASB supplies “the burden.”
